claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has an α + β dual-phase microstructure.
Untreated TC4 has relatively low inherent hardness and suboptimal wear resistance.
Untreated TC4 has a coarse α + β microstructure.
Exposing pre-polished TC4 to nitrogen at approximately 900°C for 10 hours followed by controlled cooling will promote formation of a uniform TiN surface layer.
Process optimization, pre-treatment, and controlled cooling can ensure uniformity and adhesion of the nitride layer while confining modification to the surface.
Gas nitriding under the proposed conditions will produce a hardened, uniformly thick TiN-enriched surface layer.
The nitrided surface will contain a controlled nitrogen concentration gradient transitioning into an unmodified dual-phase core.
At high temperature, nitrogen diffuses into the TC4 surface.
Diffused nitrogen reacts with titanium to form TiN.
The TiN phase significantly increases surface hardness.
Higher surface hardness reduces wear by impeding material removal and debris formation under high contact stress.
Surface-localized nitriding leaves the underlying ductile α + β structure intact.
The treated surface may exhibit a three- to fivefold local hardness increase relative to untreated TC4.
The treated samples will have a markedly lower wear rate than untreated TC4.
The bulk ductility and toughness of treated TC4 will remain unchanged.
The improvement is conditional on the service temperature remaining well below 900°C and the nitride layer remaining intact.
Hardness and wear improvements depend critically on precise control of nitriding parameters, layer uniformity, and adhesion.
